key_insight: Introducing attribute tokens that disentangle and parametrically encode multiple lighting factors enables precise, continuous control of image illumination within a conditional image-generation framework.
problem_solved: Existing relighting methods struggle to offer fine-grained, independent control over multiple illumination attributes (intensity, color, ambient, diffuse, 3D light position) and often rely on expensive inverse rendering or limited, discrete edits.
method: Formulate relighting as a conditional image-generation task and condition the generator on learned attribute tokens representing distinct lighting factors (intensity, color, ambient, diffuse, 3D positions).

Train on a large-scale synthetic dataset with ground-truth lighting annotations and a small set of real images to improve realism; enforce token supervision to achieve disentanglement and continuous interpolation of lighting attributes.
Use token-based conditioning at generation time to apply user-specified continuous edits (sliders) or combinations of attributes for precise relighting control.
impact: Gives practitioners a practical, interpretable way to perform fine-grained, controllable relighting for photography, AR/VR, data augmentation, and lighting-aware model training—without full inverse rendering pipelines.
visual_elements: Before / after image grid showing independent edits of intensity, color, ambient, diffuse, and light position (with corresponding slider icons).
Architecture diagram: image encoder + attribute tokens -> conditional generator, highlighting token injection points and supervision signals.
Interpolation strip: continuous token interpolation producing smooth lighting transitions to demonstrate controllability.
Dataset composition chart: synthetic vs. real images and examples of ground-truth lighting annotations used for training.
paper_title: TokenLight: Precise Lighting Control in Images using Attribute Tokens
paper_authors: Sumit Chaturvedi, Yannick Hold-Geoffroy, Mengwei Ren, Jingyuan Liu, He Zhang
